entities.summary:
The Croatian National Guard was an armed force established by Croatia in April and May 1991 during the Croatian War of Independence. Although it was established within the framework of the Ministry of the Interior for legal reasons, the ZNG was under the direct command of the Ministry of Defence. It was tasked with the protection of Croatia's borders and territory, and with tasks normally associated with police forces.

The ZNG was formed with the transfer of special police units to the ZNG, establishing four all-professional brigades in May 1991, and was presented to the public in a military parade in Zagreb on 28 May. Croatian National Guard is a military branch in Europe, established in 1991-04-18. Relevant to cause-and-effect analysis.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: The Croatian National Guard played a crucial role in Croatia's independence from Yugoslavia, with its establishment and actions contributing to the country's sovereignty and territorial integrity. The ZNG's presence helped deter Yugoslav People's Army aggression and protected key cities during the war.
